q: 1. The type of canal meant for diversion of flood waters of river is .............
explain: Inundation canals do not have a permanent headwork (like a weir or barrage) and only draw water when the river level rises during floods.

q: 2. An irrigation canal which is designed to irrigate all round the year may be called .............
explain: Perennial canals are supplied by a permanent source (like a dam or a river with a weir) that ensures water availability throughout the year, including the dry season.

q: 3. Canals which are excavated directly from the rivers with or without head regulator are called .............
explain: Inundation canals are simple channels dug from the river bank to divert floodwater without the complex masonry control structures found in perennial systems.

q: 4. According to Kennedy's theory the silt is kept in suspension due to the eddies generated from .............
explain: Kennedy assumed that the upward force (eddies) keeping silt in suspension is generated only from the bed of the canal, not the sides.

q: 5. The counter berm for a canal is provided .............
options: to increase the stability of the bank
to increase the cross-sectional area of the canal
to contain the saturation gradient line within the bank
to be used as an inspection track
explain: A counter berm is an extra horizontal strip of earth added to the outer slope of a canal bank to ensure the seepage (phreatic) line does not exit the bank face, preventing erosion and failure.

q: 6. Gibb's module is a type of .............
explain: Gibb's module is a rigid module because it maintains a constant discharge regardless of the water level fluctuations in either the distributary or the field channel.

q: 7. In the case of a notch type of canal fall, the surplus energy is dissipated .............
explain: In notch falls, a water cushion (cistern) is provided at the downstream bed level to absorb the impact and dissipate the energy of the falling water.

q: 8. A canal escape is a structure constructed for the purpose of .............
options: discharging waste water from the canal
explain: An escape acts as a 'safety valve' for the canal, allowing excess water (from rain or sudden closure of outlets) to be discharged safely into a natural drain.

q: 9. Syphon aqueduct is selected as the cross drainage work when the canal bed level .............
options: is below the maximum flood level in the drain
is above the maximum flood level in the drain
is below the bed level of the drain
explain: If the canal bed is lower than the High Flood Level (HFL) of the drain, the drain water must be depressed and passed under pressure (syphonic action) beneath the canal.

q: 10. The length of water way required for the drain at a cross drainage work is obtained as .............
explain: According to Lacey's regime perimeter formula, the waterway (L) is given by $4.75\sqrt{Q}$, where Q is the maximum flood discharge.

q: 11. The difference in elevations of top of bank and full supply level of a canal is called .............
explain: Freeboard is the vertical distance provided as a safety margin to prevent water from overtopping the banks due to waves or sudden discharge increases.

q: 12. The full supply level of a canal at its head regulator should be kept .............
options: at the same F.S.L. of parent canal
15 cm below the F.S.L. of parent canal
15 cm above the F.S.L. of parent canal
explain: To ensure a smooth gravity flow into the off-take canal even during slight fluctuations, the F.S.L. of the off-take is typically kept 15 cm to 30 cm lower than the parent canal.

q: 13. The difference between the level of the top of the bank and the F.S.L. is known as .............
explain: Freeboard is the safety vertical distance provided to prevent overtopping of the banks due to waves, sudden discharge increases, or wind action.

q: 14. The minimum free board to be provided should be 90 cm if the discharge in the canal is between .............
explain: As discharge increases, the risk of wave height and surge increases. Standards recommend a 0.9m freeboard for discharges in the range of 60 to 150 cumecs.

q: 15. A canal has a length of L km and the perimeter of its cross-section is P m. The amount required to line the canal, if the cost of lining per sq. m is C, will be .............
explain: Area to be lined = Perimeter (P) x Length (L). Converting L km to meters: $L \times 1000$. Total Cost = $P \times (L \times 1000) \times C = 1000 PLC$.

q: 16. A triangular channel section has side slopes of 1 vertical : z horizontal. If the depth of flow is y, what is the hydraulic depth?
explain: Hydraulic Depth (D) = Area / Top Width. For a triangle: $Area = z y^2$; $Top Width = 2zy$. $D = (zy^2) / (2zy) = y/2$.

q: 17. The most desirable section for a lined canal is .............
options: trapezoidal with rounded corners for large sections
triangular with round bottom for small sections
explain: Rounded corners reduce friction and prevent silt deposition in corners. Trapezoidal is best for large flows, while triangular is efficient for small discharges.

q: 18. The uplift pressure on the roof of an inverted siphon will be maximum when .............
explain: The roof of an inverted siphon (where the drain passes under the canal) experiences maximum upward force when the drain is at its High Flood Level (HFL), exerting maximum hydrostatic pressure.

q: 19. The crest level of a barrage is kept .............
options: almost at the river bed level with large gates
explain: Unlike a weir, a barrage keeps its crest low (near river bed level) to offer less obstruction to floods. The ponding of water is achieved almost entirely by large adjustable gates.

q: 20. Stone pitching, or any other material laid on a sloping face of an earthen bank to maintain its slope or to protect it from erosion is called
explain: Revetment is a facing of stone, concrete units, or slabs built to protect a scarp, the foot of a cliff, or a bank against erosion by wave action or currents.

q: 21. A weir in which the tail water level is more than the crest level is called
explain: A weir is considered submerged or 'drowned' when the water level on the downstream side (tail water) rises above the elevation of the weir crest.

q: 22. In Montague type fall
explain: The Montague fall is characterized by a profile following a parabolic curve, which helps in increasing the velocity and ensuring the formation of a hydraulic jump for energy dissipation.

q: 23. In the case of flow over a rectangular suppressed weir, the pressure underneath the nappe will be
explain: In suppressed weirs, air cannot enter the space under the nappe. As water carries away air, a partial vacuum (negative pressure) is created, which can cause the nappe to 'cling'.

q: 24. A canal aligned at right angles to contour of a country, is known as
explain: Side slope canals run roughly at right angles to the contours.

q: 25. The berms when fully formed
options: reduce the absorption losses and prevents leaks
protect the bank from erosion because of wave action
provide a scope for future widening the channel
explain: Berms collect silt over time, which helps in lining the canal naturally (reducing seepage) and strengthening the banks.

q: 26. The borrow pits should, preferably, be taken from
options: the field on the right side of canal
the field on the left side of the canal
the central half width of the section of the canal
explain: Taking borrow pits from the canal bed (central width) is preferred because they will eventually fill with silt, making the canal bed smoother.

q: 27. Lining of a canal
options: increases available head for power generation
explain: A lined canal is more stable, loses less water to seepage, and maintains a steeper energy gradient useful for small-scale hydro projects.

q: 28. Kennedy, in his silt theory, assumed that the silt is kept in suspension because of eddies generated from the
explain: Kennedy's theory simplified the mechanics by assuming only the vertical eddies rising from the canal bed support the silt particles.

q: 29. Lacey assumed that silt is kept in suspension because of the normal components of eddies generated from the
explain: Lacey's theory improved upon Kennedy's by stating that eddies arise from the whole perimeter, including the sides.

q: 30. If m is the mean particle diameter of the silt in mm, the Lacey's silt factor (f) is given by
explain: The silt factor $f$ determines the roughness and required velocity of the channel based on the bed material size.

q: 31. The Sarda canal has a
explain: The Sarda type fall is a classic example of a vertical drop fall, used when the discharge is small and the drop is around 1 to 1.5 meters.

q: 32. The relation for discharge (Q) over a rectangular crest of a Sarda fall is
explain: This is the modified weir formula used for the rectangular crest design of a Sarda type fall.

q: 33. A baffle wall is a sort of low weir constructed at the end of the cistern to
options: head up water to its upstream to such a high that hydraulic jump is formed
withstand the actual impact of the high velocity jet to dissipate the energy
explain: The baffle wall (or baffle platform) helps ensure the hydraulic jump occurs within the paved cistern to protect the bed.

q: 34. A device which ensures a constant discharge of water passing from one channel to another irrespective of water level in each within certain specified limits, is called
explain: This is the definition of a rigid module, which provides a constant discharge regardless of water level fluctuations.

q: 35. In a flexible outlet, the discharge depends upon the
options: difference of water level between distributary and water course
explain: A semi-module (flexible outlet) depends only on the water level in the parent distributary, not on the field channel level.

q: 36. When discharge of an outlet is independent of the water levels in the water course and the distributary, the outlet is termed as a
explain: A rigid module is designed to provide a fixed flow rate even if water levels change in either channel.

q: 37. The ratio of the head recovered to the head put in an outlet, is called
explain: Efficiency of an outlet refers to how much energy (head) is maintained after the water passes through the module.

q: 38. The sensitivity of a rigid module is ............
explain: A rigid module maintains a constant discharge regardless of the water level in the distributary or the watercourse; therefore, its sensitivity to changes in the supply level is zero.

q: 39. The flexibility of a hyper-proportional outlet is .......... one.
explain: An outlet is hyper-proportional when its flexibility is greater than unity, meaning the discharge of the outlet changes more rapidly than the discharge of the distributary.

q: 40. When the difference in weir crest and downstream river bed is limited into 3 meters, the weir generally used is .............
explain: For moderate drops (up to 3m), a concrete slope (or glacis) weir is preferred to safely guide the water and dissipate energy.

q: 41. In Bligh's creep theory .............
options: there is no distinction between horizontal and vertical creep
loss of head does not take place in the same proportion as creep length
the uplift pressure distribution is not linear, but follows a sine curve
explain: Unlike Lane's theory, Bligh's theory treats horizontal and vertical creep paths as equally effective in reducing head loss.

q: 42. For smooth entry, the regulators are aligned at an angle of ............. to the water.
explain: Aligning the head regulator at an angle of 110° to the weir/barrage axis helps in smooth entry of water and effectively reduces silt entry into the canal.

q: 43. The level of a canal diversion head work depends upon .............
explain: The pond level is the most critical factor as it must be high enough to ensure the required Full Supply Level (FSL) in the canal even during low river flow.

q: 44. When the drain is over the canal, the structure provided is known as .............
explain: A super-passage is the opposite of an aqueduct; here, the natural drainage (stream) is carried in a trough across and above the canal.

q: 45. Lacey's regime condition is obtained if .............
options: silt grade in the channel is variable
discharge in the channel is variable
silt charge in the channel is variable
channel flows in unlimited, incoherent alluvium of the same character as that transported material
explain: Lacey's theory assumes the channel is flowing in an infinite depth of the same material it is transporting (incoherent alluvium).

q: 46. The scour depth D of a river during flood, may be calculated from the Lacey's equation .............
explain: The regime scour depth ($R$) for a wide channel is given by $R = 0.47 (Q/f)^{1/3}$.

q: 47. Finally formed berms in canals are provided for .............
options: protection of banks erosion by the waves
explain: Berms act as a buffer, reducing wave impact, providing space for sediment to settle (which seals the banks), and widening the bank base for stability.

q: 48. An outlet which maintains a constant discharge irrespective of fluctuation in the water levels of supplying channel or water course, is known as .............
explain: Rigid modules (like the Gibb's module) are designed to provide a fixed discharge regardless of the water levels in the parent canal or the field channel.

q: 49. The sensitivity of a rigid module, is .............
explain: Sensitivity is the ratio of change in outlet discharge to change in canal level. Since a rigid module's discharge is constant, its sensitivity is zero.

q: 50. Bligh's theory of seepage assumes .............
options: equal weightage to the horizontal and vertical creep
more weightage to horizontal creep than vertical creep
less weightage to horizontal creep than vertical creep
loss of head following the sine curve
explain: Bligh's Creep Theory famously makes no distinction between horizontal and vertical creep paths regarding head loss.

q: 51. Process of meandering is due to .............
options: discharge and hydraulic properties of streams
relative erodibility of the bed and banks
explain: Meandering is the result of excess energy in the flow interacting with erodible banks and varying sediment loads.

q: 52. The downstream expansion head of a guide bank is extended to subtend an angle at the center, equal to .............
explain: For efficient flow expansion downstream, a guide bank is usually curved with an arc subtending 45 degrees.
